1c9a5d5e71.what_happened: The White House withdrew Dr. Heidi Overton’s nomination to lead the FDA a day before a Senate health committee vote. Overton, a physician and abortion opponent with strong Trump ties, faced bipartisan concerns over her stance on vaccines and scientific independence. Reproductive rights groups celebrated the withdrawal, warning about future anti‑abortion nominees.
details: The White House dropped Overton’s nomination after Trump nominated her in August. Overton, a physician and prominent abortion opponent, has spent most of her career working for Trump or conservative groups. Her nomination was seen as a move to bring a stabilizing Trump loyalist to the agency after a tumultuous year under Trump’s first FDA commissioner, Marty Makary.

Overton faced bipartisan Senate questions about her willingness to break from Trump, especially his unsupported claims about childhood vaccine dangers. Republican Senator Bill Cassidy of Louisiana, who chairs the Senate health committee, remained undecided ahead of Wednesday’s committee vote. Cassidy had previously called Overton’s support for breaking up combination vaccines “almost disqualifying” and pressed her on scientific independence during a September hearing.

A reproductive rights group praised the withdrawal. Mini Timmaraju, president and CEO of Reproductive Freedom for All, said Overton posed a serious threat to medication abortion access and warned about future nominees. Overton’s 2023 policy brief urged strict regulation of the abortion pill mifeprestone and criticized mailing of abortion pills. To be confirmed, Overton would have needed all 12 Republican votes on the committee; Democrats hold 11 seats. Republicans are racing to confirm Trump’s remaining nominees before the Senate Democrats take power in January.

1c9a5d5e71.whats_next: Republicans are working to confirm the rest of Trump’s nominees before the new Congress hands power to Senate Democrats in January.

1c9a5d5e71.spoken: Here’s what’s happening on the political scene today. The White House has pulled the plug on Dr. Heidi Overton’s bid to lead the Food and Drug Administration, just one day before a crucial vote in the Senate health committee. Overton, a physician who has long opposed abortion and has ties to former President Trump’s inner circle, faced tough questions from lawmakers about her independence, especially regarding Trump’s claims about childhood vaccines. Republican Senator Bill Cassidy of Louisiana, who chairs the committee, says he’s still undecided, having previously called her support for breaking up combination vaccines “almost disqualifying.” Reproductive rights groups are cheering the withdrawal, warning that another anti‑abortion nominee could threaten medication abortion access. Meanwhile, Republicans are racing to confirm the rest of Trump’s nominees before the new Congress takes over in January.

69b783e088.what_happened: Donald Trump will attend the APEC summit in Shenzhen, China, this week and is expected to meet Xi Jinping and hold a three-way meeting with Vladimir Putin. The talks are expected to focus on AI regulation, trade and Taiwan, with little chance of major breakthroughs. The summit follows Democrats winning control of Congress and comes amid scrutiny over Jensen Huang and alleged spy Alice Huang.
details: Donald Trump, the United States president, will attend the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in Shenzhen, China, this week, where 21 Pacific Rim member economies are taking part. He is expected to meet Chinese President Xi Jinping and to hold a three-way meeting with Xi and Russian President Vladimir Putin. A Trump-Xi meeting on the sidelines would be the third time the two leaders have met this year, after Xi hosted Trump in Beijing in May and Trump hosted Xi at the White House in September, with earlier meetings heavy on ceremony, aimed at showing stability in a consequential relationship, and light on meaningful breakthroughs.

Experts predicted a similar approach in Shenzhen, with AI regulation, trade and the self-ruling island of Taiwan likely to loom large. The summit comes just days after Democrats won commanding control of both chambers of the US Congress, a shift that will likely serve as a major check on Trump in his final two years, while Beijing is increasingly looking beyond the Trump era to see what comes next. Ali Wyne, a senior research and advocacy adviser on US-China relations at Crisis Group, said Trump will work to strengthen his rapport with Xi but the meeting is unlikely to produce substantive breakthroughs, Yury Ushakov, Putin's foreign policy adviser, told reporters on Monday that the significance and symbolism of the meetings between the three superpower leaders are hard to overestimate, neither side has released a formal agenda for the expected Trump-Xi meeting, and the White House said the countries will support each other at APEC and at the G20 summit in Florida in December and agreed to build a constructive relationship of strategic stability based on respect, fairness and reciprocity.

AI regulation is set to loom large, with the US and China, as industry leaders, facing pressure to jointly agree safeguards on the transformative technology, after both sides pledged in September to set up a mechanism to quickly communicate AI-related incidents and hold a dialogue on emerging risks. The Trump administration has repeatedly downplayed the need to integrate developmental guardrails, Trump said after the White House meeting that the US would not be putting on brakes on the AI industry, and Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, speaking at a National Committee on US-China Relations event last week, said both sides expect to exchange best practices for evaluating and testing advanced models before their release and for keeping human judgment firmly in command of this technology, while adding that they should harbour no illusions about the differences between the United States and China and that their approach to every challenge will not always converge. The recent resignation of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, which followed revelations that he had an affair with an alleged Chinese spy, will also loom large over any Trump-Xi meeting even if it is not directly addressed, because Huang's close relationship with Trump, including accompanying the US president to Beijing during his May visit, and his ties to alleged spy Alice Huang have renewed questions about the influence he exerted over the US government as he pushed to ease restrictions on the sale of advanced AI chips to Beijing; Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick has faced particular scrutiny, including from prominent members of the Republican Party, over his reportedly lax enforcement of export controls related to China, and Crisis Group's Wyne said Trump will be under enormous pressure from Congress and members of his own administration to raise the scandal and warn Xi that their relationship could suffer if Trump concludes that Xi has been deploying Huang and other prominent business executives to sabotage US artificial intelligence efforts; some experts expect it to have little bearing on his interaction with his Chinese counterpart, and Gabriel Wildau, managing director at the advisory firm Teneo, told Al Jazeera last week that Trump shows no sign that he intends to disrupt the current US-China rapprochement; the Reuters news agency reported on Friday that US officials said Trump is not expected to raise the issue of Alice Huang with Xi, and China has denied Alice Huang was working as a spy on its behalf.

Trump has already bucked longstanding US policy on Taiwan during his recent meeting with Xi. Following the Beijing summit in May, Trump told reporters he had discussed US arms sales to the self-governing island, which Beijing claims as its own, in great detail with the Chinese president, even though the US has provided arms to Taiwan since 1979 as mandated under the Taiwan Relations Act and, under the 1982 Six Assurances document, Washington has not consulted with China on such sales. In a subsequent Fox News interview, Trump referred to Taiwan as a very good negotiating chip with China and has since held up approval of a $14bn arms package earmarked for the island, while Bonnie Glaser and Noah Munk of the German Marshall Fund of the United States (GMF) wrote that the language invites Beijing to expect something in return for each future approval and that the more successful the bargaining appears, the more Beijing will press it and treat the next notification as a concession from Washington rather than a routine measure under the Taiwan Relations Act; the White House defended the delay by citing limited production capacity, particularly amid the US-Israel war with Iran, and the delicate nature of the US-China trade truce, and Democratic control of Congress plus general bipartisan support for Taiwan could see pressure increase on the issue in Trump's final two years.
69b783e088.why_it_matters: The article calls the US-China relationship consequential and says the summit follows Democrats winning control of Congress, a likely check on Trump.

69b783e088.spoken: President Donald Trump is heading to Shenzhen, China, this week for the APEC summit, which includes 21 Pacific Rim economies, where he is expected to meet Chinese President Xi Jinping and also hold a three way meeting with Russian President Vladimir Putin. It would be Trump and Xi's third meeting this year, after Beijing in May and the White House in September, but experts expect more ceremony than breakthroughs. AI regulation, trade and Taiwan are likely to dominate, along with the recent resignation of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and questions about alleged Chinese spy Alice Huang. 2ce8ea0932.what_happened: A malicious cyber attack targeted nearly 200 major websites, including the BBC, HSBC UAE, Air France and IKEA. Hackers injected corrupted JavaScript code into Optimizely tools, affecting about 178 sites. The attackers aimed to steal credit card numbers and cryptocurrency and to infect Apple devices.
details: Hackers injected corrupted JavaScript code into tools hosted by Optimizely, a digital platform used by major companies to customize online experiences. This malicious cyber attack targeted nearly 200 major websites, including the BBC, HSBC UAE, Air France and IKEA, as well as Zoom, CNN, Salesforce, GitLab, Equifax, Air France-KLM, Ledger and Peacock. The attack was reported Tuesday by specialist media.

The attackers sought to steal users’ credit card numbers and cryptocurrency and to upload code to Apple devices for further exploitation. According to security researcher Scott Helme, the attacker’s crypto wallets received about $7,040 within roughly nine hours on November 16. Helme first uncovered the hack and wrote about it on his blog Monday.

Most of the malicious code had been removed from the affected sites, Helme said. Optimizely stated that it identified and contained a security incident affecting some of its Web Experimentation customers. The company added that the vulnerable path was blocked, the injected code was removed, and customers were contacted directly.

107e8327fe.what_happened: Pew Research Center report released on Tuesday projects that Islam will become the world’s largest religion by 2035, overtaking Christianity. The study covers 201 countries and territories from 2020 to 2070 and finds that Muslims will grow faster than Christians. It estimates Muslims could gain 1.6 billion people through natural increase, compared with 792 million for Christians.
details: The Pew Research Center, in a report released on Tuesday and reported by Al Jazeera, projects that Islam will become the world’s largest religion by 2035, overtaking Christianity. The study covers 201 countries and territories, representing 99.98 percent of the global population, and examines seven religious groups from 2020 to 2070. It is part of the Pew‑Templeton Global Religious Futures Project and warns that the findings are not intended to predict all possible future changes.

According to the report, Muslims have the highest fertility rate at 3.1 children per woman, which Pew says is one of the factors making them the world’s fastest‑growing religious group, while Christians have the second‑highest at 2.5, above the replacement level of about 2.1. Both groups are expected to keep pace with overall world population growth, with Muslims potentially gaining 1.6 billion people through natural increase compared to 792 million for Christians. The study also projects a net loss of 8 million Muslims and 105 million Christians due to people joining or leaving the faiths, and notes that the number of Muslims converting to Christianity is only slightly greater than the reverse.

The report finds that most of the projected growth in the Muslim population will occur in countries where Muslims already form a majority, including 53 countries that are expected to gain an additional 1.2 billion Muslims by 2070, representing 74 percent of the total growth. By 2070, Muslims are projected to make up 95 percent of the population in the Middle East‑North Africa region and to surpass the religiously unaffiliated in the Asia‑Pacific region, while Pakistan’s Muslim population is expected to double from 227 million in 2020 to 461 million in 2070, overtaking Indonesia. Christian growth will be concentrated in 120 countries where Christians are already the majority, with an overall increase of 630 million, accounting for 92 percent of global Christian growth.

Christian growth concentrated in 120 majority‑Christian countries, rise by 630 million.

The study covers 201 countries and territories and examines seven religious groups from 2020 to 2070. It finds that Muslims have a fertility rate of 3.1 children per woman, compared to 2.5 for Christians, and that both groups are expected to grow. The report estimates Muslims could gain 1.6 billion people through natural increase, while Christians would gain 792 million. It also projects a net loss of 8 million Muslims and 105 million Christians. Most Muslim growth will occur in majority‑Muslim countries, and by 2070 Muslims could make up 95 percent of the Middle East and North Africa region. Pakistan's Muslim population is expected to double to 461 million, overtaking Indonesia. Christian growth will be concentrated in 120 majority‑Christian countries, rising by 630 million.

853098c5ff.what_happened: A suspect has been arrested over the assault of a private bus driver in Dambulla. The attack happened on November 14 in front of the main bus stand, and footage of it circulated on social media. The suspect, from Pohoranwewa in Dambulla, was arrested yesterday (18) and is to be produced before court today (19).
details: Police say the assault took place on November 14 in front of the main bus stand in Dambulla. It involved the driver of a private bus travelling from Kandy to Polonnaruwa, who was injured in the attack.
The injured driver lodged a complaint with Police while receiving treatment at the Dambulla Hospital. The arrest came after footage of the incident circulated on social media.

After investigations, officers of the Dambulla Headquarters Police used CCTV footage of the incident to identify the suspect. The suspect, a resident of Pohoranwewa in Dambulla, was arrested yesterday (18).
He is scheduled to be produced before court today (19). The Dambulla Headquarters Police are conducting further investigations.

b1b2e9f976.what_happened: Sri Lankan troops serving with the international Gang Suppression Force joined Haiti's National Police in a pre-dawn raid on November 15 against the Kokorat San Ras gang in Gros-Morne, Artibonite. The joint forces freed a church and a school held by gang members, seized weapons and motorcycles, and cleared roads blocked for years. Haitian Prime Minister Alix Didier Fils-Aimé praised the operation on X.
details: On November 15, Sri Lankan personnel serving under the international Gang Suppression Force (GSF) took part in a joint anti-gang operation with the Haitian National Police (PNH) in the Artibonite region. The pre-dawn raid targeted strongholds of the armed Kokorat San Ras gang in the Tibwadòm and Carnifice areas of Gros-Morne.

During the mission, the joint forces cleared and secured a church and a school that gang members had occupied. They seized firearms, ammunition, and motorcycles, and dismantled barricades and trenches that were blocking National Road 5. This cleared key roadways that had been blocked for years.

Haitian Prime Minister Alix Didier Fils-Aimé praised the coordinated operation in a post on X, commending the PNH, GSF and Sri Lankan troops. Sri Lankan personnel are stationed across key operational hubs including Port-au-Prince, Gonaïves, and Estrella. There they conduct armoured vehicle patrols, safeguard vital supply routes, and support local authorities in dismantling organized crime networks and restoring stability for affected civilian communities.
b1b2e9f976.why_it_matters: The raid reopened roads that had been blocked for years and helped restore stability for local communities affected by gangs.

b1b2e9f976.spoken: Sri Lankan soldiers serving in Haiti have earned praise from the country's Prime Minister after a big anti-gang mission. On November fifteenth, these troops, part of an international Gang Suppression Force, joined Haiti's National Police for a pre-dawn raid in the Artibonite region. They targeted a gang called Kokorat San Ras in the Gros-Morne area. During the operation, the forces took back a church and a school that gang members had occupied, seized guns, ammunition and motorcycles, and tore down barricades and trenches. That cleared National Road Five, which had been blocked for years. Prime Minister Alix Didier Fils-Aimé thanked everyone involved in a post on X. The Sri Lankan teams are based in places like Port-au-Prince and Gonaïves, where they patrol in armoured vehicles, protect supply routes, and help local police break up organized crime and bring stability back to communities.

74ca8fa46a.what_happened: The Department of Motor Traffic will require prior appointments for all public services at its Narahenpita Head Office starting November 23, 2026. Daily appointment slots have been more than doubled to serve more people faster. People can book by phone or online and are asked not to queue outside early in the morning.
details: The Department of Motor Traffic announced that from November 23, 2026, all public services at the Narahenpita Head Office will be provided only through a prior appointment system. Members of the public must book a date and time in advance. The department has increased daily appointment slots by more than double to handle more service seekers and ensure faster, more convenient delivery.

You can book an appointment by calling 011 2 117 116 or by visiting the department's online booking portal at https://dmtappointments.dmt.gov.lk. The public is urged not to queue unnecessarily outside the office from early morning beginning on that date. The Commissioner General of Motor Traffic, retired Air Vice Marshal Thushara Fernando, explained that the new system aims to improve public convenience and reduce waiting times.
He asked everyone seeking services at the Narahenpita Head Office to book ahead so they do not face inconvenience. The announcement came from Newswire.

28fefe16db.what_happened: California has issued an investigative subpoena to AI chip designer Nvidia following the departure of its longtime CEO Jensen Huang. Attorney General Rob Bonta is investigating whether Nvidia or Huang helped China obtain advanced chips or secret information, potentially misleading investors and the public.
details: California's top law enforcement official, Rob Bonta, announced on Thursday that the state is examining if corporate securities laws were violated by misleading the public and investors. The inquiry centers on Nvidia, which is based in Santa Clara, California, amidst what Bonta called a messy transnational situation regarding advanced tech transfers to China.

The investigation follows revelations earlier this month that former CEO and co-founder Jensen Huang had an extramarital affair with Alice Huang, a suspected Chinese spy and executive at Singapore data center firm Megaspeed. Megaspeed is a major Nvidia customer, and US lawmakers have asked the Department of Commerce to probe if it diverted chips to China, though Megaspeed claims such allegations lack verifiable proof.

Huang admitted to extramarital affairs and stepped down last week following claims of relationships with subordinates. Nvidia board chair Harvey Jones stated the company will not reinstate Huang, even though Huang stated he would be honored to return and tech figures like Elon Musk supported him, while company shares have plunged 22% since the affair was reported in early November.
28fefe16db.why_it_matters: The probe examines whether Nvidia violated state corporate securities laws by misleading investors and the public regarding confidential information or advanced chips reaching China.

details: The source is a Newswire report. A 36-year-old man was arrested for allegedly having ICE narcotics. He died after suddenly becoming ill while held at the Matale Police Station early today (20).

18ccc76ffe.what_happened: The Court of Appeal emphasised that elephants must be safeguarded as a vital national resource and heritage. The bench made this observation while hearing a legal challenge against a government policy permitting firearms for farmers. The court noted that international tourists visit Sri Lanka to see wildlife rather than large buildings.
details: The Sri Lanka Wildlife and Nature Protection Society filed a petition asking the court to overturn the government's decision to issue guns to farmers for crop protection. The case was heard on Tuesday by Court of Appeal President Justice Rohitha Abeysuriya and Justice Priyantha Fernando. The petitioner's lawyer, President's Counsel Sanjeewa Jayawardena, warned that giving firearms to farmers seriously imperils wild animals, especially elephants, noting that the tusker Kawanthissa had already been shot dead.

Jayawardena informed the judges that the minimum landholding required to obtain a firearm had recently been reduced by the government from five acres to two acres, which could lead to many more weapons being handed out. He revealed that 305 firearms were distributed by 2002, 490 by 2026, and data indicated a total of 3,207 firearms have been issued so far.

Justice Abeysuriya stated that the court places significant weight on protecting the environment and wildlife, stressing that elephants are a national asset and that tourists do not travel to the island for tall buildings. The court said it would seek proposals from all parties on ways to keep elephants safe. Named respondents include Deputy Defence Minister retired Major General Aruna Jayasekara, Defence Ministry Secretary Air Vice Marshal Sampath Thuyacontha, and Environment Minister Dr. Dammika Patabendi.
18ccc76ffe.why_it_matters: The case highlights concerns that loosening rules on issuing firearms to farmers puts endangered wildlife, particularly the national elephant population, at severe risk.
key_facts: The Court of Appeal considered a petition against issuing firearms to farmers to guard crops.
Court President Justice Rohitha Abeysuriya said foreign tourists visit for nature, not large buildings.
The land eligibility threshold for getting a firearm was lowered from five acres to two acres.
Lawyer Sanjeewa Jayawardena noted that 3,207 firearms have reportedly been issued so far.

The petitioner highlighted the fatal shooting of the tusker Kawanthissa.
Court adjourned the matter until November 30 to seek safety proposals.
18ccc76ffe.whats_next: The Court of Appeal will obtain submissions from all parties on measures to safeguard elephants and will continue hearing the petition on November 30.
18ccc76ffe.blurb: Sri Lanka's Court of Appeal has called for elephant protection, saying tourists visit for wildlife, not large buildings.
18ccc76ffe.spoken: Sri Lanka's Court of Appeal has stepped in to stress the vital importance of protecting the nation's wild elephants. While hearing a legal challenge against a government decision to hand out firearms to farmers, Court President Justice Rohitha Abeysuriya remarked that foreign tourists come to Sri Lanka to experience its natural heritage, not to look at large buildings. The court heard that authorities lowered the land size needed to get a gun from five acres down to two, and over three thousand firearms have already been distributed. With animals like the tusker Kawanthissa recently shot dead, wildlife advocates want the policy scrapped. The judges will collect safety ideas from all sides and resume hearings on November 30.
18ccc76ffe.subject: Elephant protection

6a7f3a3a3d.what_happened: Parliament passed the second reading of the 2027 Budget by a 97-vote majority following a seven-day debate. The vote concluded with 157 votes in favour and 60 votes against. This is the 81st Budget in the history of Sri Lanka.
details: President Anura Kumara Dissanayake presented the proposal on November 12 in his role as Minister of Finance, Planning and Economic Development. Debate began on November 13 and finished at 6.30 pm on November 20, marking the third budget presented by the National People’s Power government. Records show 157 MPs voted in favour, 60 MPs voted against, and no MPs abstained.

The 2027 Budget estimates total government spending at Rs. 7.933 trillion, up from Rs. 7.309 trillion in revised 2026 estimates. Total revenue is projected at Rs. 6.15 trillion, while revenue and grants reach Rs. 6.18 trillion. These figures leave an estimated budget deficit of Rs. 1.753 trillion, representing 4.5% of Gross Domestic Product.

Alongside these proceedings, Central Bank Governor Dr. Nandalal Weerasinghe announced headline inflation will likely exceed 9% this month. In judicial matters, Colombo Chief Magistrate Asanga S. Bodaragama ordered a progress report on the Krrish inquiry by December 01, while MP Chamara Sampath Dassanayake was further remanded until November 27.

A 97-vote majority cleared the proposal after a seven-day parliamentary debate.
President Anura Kumara Dissanayake presented the proposal on November 12.
Government expenditure is estimated at Rs. 7.933 trillion for 2027.

After seven days of debate, one hundred and fifty-seven lawmakers voted in favour, while sixty voted against, with no abstentions. Presented by President Anura Kumara Dissanayake as Finance Minister, this is the eighty-first budget in the country's history. It outlines government spending of seven point nine three three trillion rupees and projects an estimated deficit of one point seven five three trillion rupees. Meanwhile, Central Bank Governor Dr. Nandalal Weerasinghe warned that inflation will likely top nine percent this month. Lawmakers now move to the Committee Stage debate, which continues until the final vote on December 14.

96a7f9767d.what_happened: A Missouri state court judge has approved a $7.25bn settlement by German firm Bayer to resolve lawsuits alleging its Roundup weedkiller causes cancer. The deal addresses around 65,000 claims from people who fell ill after using the product. The ruling potentially closes out litigation that has troubled the company for nearly a decade.
details: Judge Timothy Boyer of a St Louis court ruled that the $7.25bn agreement was fair, reasonable, and adequate. He rejected complaints that individual payments were too small compared to earlier settlements, warning that further delays would force cancer victims, including those who are terminally ill, to wait indefinitely for financial relief.

Originally announced in February, the settlement aims to conclude almost all existing and future Roundup cases across the country. Bayer had been confronted with roughly 65,000 lawsuits in US state and federal courts from users who alleged they developed cancer from domestic or workplace exposure.

Bayer bought Monsanto, the manufacturer of Roundup, for $63bn in 2018, which led to widespread legal battles and caused its share value to slide by 46%. Although Bayer paid $10.9bn to resolve large portions of the litigation in 2020, a previous $1.25bn plan covering future claims failed to secure court backing.

Bayer maintains that Roundup and glyphosate do not cause cancer and are supported by decades of scientific research. Five months prior to this approval, the US supreme court issued a 7-2 ruling overturning a $1.25m award to Missouri resident John Durnell, ruling that federal pesticide rules override state-level failure-to-warn claims. About 200 cases continue in federal court, outside of this agreement.
96a7f9767d.why_it_matters: The approval provides financial relief to tens of thousands of cancer patients while removing a massive legal risk that has depressed Bayer's stock by 46% since 2018.
key_facts: Judge Timothy Boyer approved Bayer's $7.25bn Roundup settlement in St Louis, Missouri.
The agreement addresses about 65,000 lawsuits linking the weedkiller to cancer.
Bayer bought Monsanto for $63bn in 2018, after which its share price fell 46%.
Bayer previously settled widespread Roundup claims for $10.9bn back in 2020.

Plaintiffs' lawyer Christopher Seeger noted the supreme court decision limited victims' court options.
About 200 pending federal cases are excluded from this settlement.
96a7f9767d.whats_next: Lawyers aim to distribute the settlement funds to Roundup victims as quickly as possible, while Bayer continues to defend roughly 200 pending federal lawsuits.
96a7f9767d.blurb: A Missouri judge has approved Bayer's $7.25bn settlement over claims that its Roundup weedkiller causes cancer.
96a7f9767d.spoken: A major legal battle in the United States has reached a critical turning point. A state judge in St Louis, Missouri, has officially approved Bayer's seven point two five billion dollar settlement over its Roundup weedkiller. The German company has faced around sixty-five thousand claims from people who say using the product at home or at work gave them cancer. Judge Timothy Boyer dismissed objections about payout amounts, noting that delaying approval would force victims, including those with terminal cancer, to wait years for compensation. Bayer has seen its stock drop forty-six percent since buying Monsanto for sixty-three billion dollars in 2018. The company insists the product is safe, and lawyers now plan to distribute the funds as swiftly as possible.
96a7f9767d.subject: Roundup cancer litigation

933288238d.what_happened: Denmark expelled Russia's defence attaché after accusing Moscow of plotting to kill Ukrainian rapper Kyivstoner at a concert near Copenhagen. Police arrested three men with firearms and knives five minutes before the scheduled performance, which was cancelled. Two Danish men were charged with attempted murder and assisting a foreign intelligence service.
details: Denmark summoned the Russian ambassador and announced the expulsion of Russia's defence attaché within seven days, with Foreign Minister Lars Løkke Rasmussen stating that they have exposed Russia. He also said Denmark is considering suspending Schengen visas for Russians and is working with the EU to tighten visa rules.

PET assessed that Russian intelligence planned to kill US-Ukrainian rapper Kyivstoner, whose real name is Albert Viktorovich Vasiliev, during a concert on 25 September in a Copenhagen suburb. Police stopped three men in a car near the venue north of Copenhagen with two loaded pistols and two knives at about 9.55pm, five minutes before the concert; one had bought a ticket, and the concert was cancelled, while a fourth suspect was arrested later. The suspects are linked to the banned gang Loyal to Familia, and two Danish men were charged under Section 108 with assisting a foreign intelligence service and attempted murder, denying wrongdoing.

PET head Rasmus Kieffer-Kristensen said the assassination attempt is not something previously seen in Denmark and shows Russia is increasingly aggressive and risk‑taking, adding that Russian intelligence attempted to carry out an execution in Denmark. Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen stated that Denmark faces a cornered Russia and must not waver in supporting Ukraine. European Council President Antonio Costa called the alleged attempt unacceptable and promised the EU's full backing against Russian hybrid attacks.

Russia's Foreign Ministry Maria Zakharova said Moscow will give an appropriate response, while the Russian embassy called the expulsion vengeful and claimed no evidence of Russia's involvement. Copenhagen has previously accused Russia of hybrid attacks, including a drone shutdown of Copenhagen airport in September 2025. PET also said in September that Russia was recruiting Danish citizens to help plan sabotage against Danish defence firms with ties to Ukraine, and Russia has denied involvement in such operations.
933288238d.why_it_matters: The alleged plot illustrates the threat Russia poses to Denmark and the EU, prompting diplomatic expulsions and visa restrictions.

FM Lars Løkke Rasmussen announced the decision and visa suspension plans.

EU Council President Costa called the plot unacceptable and promised full backing.
Russia's embassy called the expulsion vengeful and denied involvement.

933288238d.blurb: Denmark expels Russian defence attaché over alleged plot to kill Ukrainian rapper Kyivstoner at Copenhagen concert.
933288238d.spoken: Good morning, listeners. In a significant diplomatic development, Denmark has expelled Russia's defence attaché after accusing Moscow of plotting to kill the Ukrainian rapper Kyivstoner at a concert near Copenhagen. The rapper, who holds both Ukrainian and U.S. citizenship, was scheduled to perform on September 25th, but police arrested three men with firearms and knives just before the show, leading to its cancellation. Danish intelligence says the plot was linked to a banned gang and Russian intelligence services. Foreign Minister Lars Løkke Rasmussen announced the expulsion and said Denmark is considering suspending Schengen visas for Russians, while working with the EU to tighten visa rules. The European Union has pledged full support, calling the alleged attempt unacceptable. Russia has threatened an appropriate response, but Denmark's prime minister insists on continuing support for Ukraine. This incident highlights the growing tensions and the importance of standing firm.
933288238d.subject: Russia-Ukraine conflict
